about.title: Monrovia Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a preventable crash upends everything, and Monrovia's own traffic figures show these losses are real, not rare: the most recent year on record counted 193 injury collisions and one traffic death across the city, with corridors like I-210, Huntington, and Foothill seeing the heaviest volume, especially during Friday's late-afternoon rush. A wrongful death claim in California is separate from any criminal proceeding and exists to help surviving family recover costs tied to the loss — funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's guidance and companionship. California law limits who may bring this claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and there's a strict two-year filing window from the date of death (shorter if a government entity is involved). LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect Monrovia families with an independent attorney, free of charge, so you're not facing these decisions without support.

whyChoose.title: Why Monrovia Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Followed Carefully
items.desc: California law limits who can file a wrongful death claim, usually starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents. An independent attorney can confirm who in your family qualifies and how the claim should be structured.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Doesn't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives surviving family two years from the date of death to file, and that window shrinks considerably if a government agency, like a city road authority, may be responsible. Connecting early helps preserve evidence tied to sites along corridors such as I-210 or Foothill before it disappears.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California allows families to seek compensation for lost financial support and for intangible losses like companionship and guidance, not just funeral costs. An attorney can help make sure both categories are properly documented and presented.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Monrovia?
items.answer: Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner, or children typically have first standing to bring the claim. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm eligibility.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the incident involved a government entity, such as a city-maintained stretch of road, that deadline can be much shorter. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may arise from the same incident. Even if criminal charges are filed, dropped, or never pursued, a family can still bring a civil claim. The two processes operate independently under California law.

items.question: Does the Friday rush-hour pattern on Monrovia roads matter to our case?
items.answer: Public crash-record patterns, like Monrovia's tendency toward more injury collisions on Friday afternoons near I-210, Huntington, and Foothill, can sometimes provide useful context when reconstructing how an incident occurred. An attorney can determine whether that kind of information is relevant to your family's specific claim.
